blocks.md: **The real value of the federal minimum wage fell in every year between 1979 and 1989, exactly as lower-tail wage inequality rose. Relative to the median, the minimum fell by about 0.38 log points over the decade (chart-read ≈), and the 10th percentile by about 0.2. Using state variation and an instrument, Autor, Manning and Smith attribute 48% of the 1979–2012 rise in the women's 50/10 gap, 11% of men's and 39% of the pooled rise to the minimum wage.**

blocks.caption: Real federal minimum wage: ≈ 7.1 in 1979, ≈ 5.2 in 1989 (chart-read; lecture's deflator), back up after the 1990–91, 1996–97 and 2007–09 increases.

blocks.md: The share of hours paid at or below the applicable minimum fell from ≈ 13% (women) and ≈ 5% (men) in 1979–81 to ≈ 4% and ≈ 3% by the mid-2000s (chart-read).

sections.heading: Counterfactual change in the 50/10 log wage gap (AMS Table 3, log points × 100)

blocks.md:
| Period, group | Observed change | Counterfactual with constant effective minimum (2SLS, levels) | Share due to the minimum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1979–1989, women | 24.6 | 11.3 | 54% |
| 1979–1989, men | 2.5 | 1.2 | 52% |
| 1979–1989, pooled | 11.8 | 6.7 | 43% |
| 1979–2012, women | 28.5 | 14.8 | 48% |
| 1979–2012, men | 7.9 | 7.0 | 11% |
| 1979–2012, pooled | 11.4 | 6.9 | 39% |

"Share due to the minimum" is (observed − counterfactual)/observed, computed here from the table. OLS counterfactuals without state fixed effects (Lee's approach) leave little or nothing to explain: −1.2 for the pooled 1979–1989 change.
